chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
For salat, there are four thousand limits. And in another narration: For salat, there are four thousand doors (chapters).

key_terms.الصلاة: Salat — the obligatory ritual prayer, one of the pillars of Islam
key_terms.باب: Bab (door/chapter) — a category or section of jurisprudential rules; the use of 'door' metaphorically implies entry points into a vast body of knowledge
key_terms.حد: Had (limit/ruling) — a fixed rule or boundary governing a religious act; in jurisprudence, a precisely defined legal prescription

ai.seo_question: How many rules does salat have according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) declares that the ritual prayer (salat) encompasses four thousand limits or — in an alternative report — four thousand chapters. This statement emphasizes the immense depth, complexity, and comprehensiveness of Islamic prayer law, suggesting that its rules, conditions, and subtleties are virtually inexhaustible. For the early Shia community, this hadith underscored the importance of scholarly expertise in fiqh and the authoritative role of the Imam as the supreme source of jurisprudential knowledge.
